content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure and the USER passage in the conversation.

**What traced cleanly.** All 16 claims trace to affirmative disclosure text: the branch-limit-below-sum premise, the per-channel contactor/current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier set, upstream branch sensing, the stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit tuple, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-reserve allocation, sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector verification, verification-interval-then-ordered-shedding, the three reclosure conditions, welded-contactor leakage threshold with inhibit plus local fault indicator, isolated local bus, offline token/last-accepted-limit operation, tamper-evident meter records, and the one-transition-at-a-time service-input mapping with store-only-on-agreement. The "reduced pilot command responsive to branch current exceeding the limit" trigger is entailed by "remains above the branch limit **after a reduced pilot command**" read with "staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond," so I did not flag it. All 25 numerals are single-meaning, appear in a figure, and match the ledger names; FIG. 4's eight shapes map one-to-one to steps 202–216 with the loop-backs matching the described flow; no section lines exist; no placeholders or unresolved alternatives remain in the application text; and the text contains no "by way of example" shape hedging.

**Two defects found**, both confined to the figure briefs — details and fixes in the structured output.

input.summary: Full preflight completed: every limitation of claims 1-16, all 25 entries in the numeral ledger and every numbered part, all four figure briefs (FIG. 1-4), the Brief Description, the detailed description, summary, background, field and abstract were traced item by item against the affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md. Claim ledger: the branch-limit-lower-than-sum premise, per-channel contactor/connector current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor, the stored charging authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit tuple, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-configurable-reserve allocation, sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector-sensor verification, verification-interval-then-ordered-shedding in a stored order, measure-after-each-open and stop-when-below, the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibit of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, the isolated local bus, network interface with signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation and token-gated new sessions, tamper-evident meter records, and the service-input one-low-energy-pilot-transition-at-a-time mapping stored only on sensor agreement all trace to exact disclosure sentences. The reduced-pilot-command trigger in claims 1 and 11 is entailed by "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval" read with "staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond", so it is treated as supported. Numerals 100-140 and 202-216 each denote one part, each appears in at least one figure brief, and the brief part names match the ledger and the description usages exactly; FIG. 4's eight shapes map one-to-one onto steps 202-216 and both return paths match the described looping; no section lines exist in this drawing set; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in the application text; and no application sentence justifies a renderer's generic outline with "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language. Two defects were found, both confined to the figure briefs: (1) FIG. 2 asserts a dedicated connector-current-sensor signal path that leaves the connector channel and crosses the isolated local bus without joining it, a connection/topology relationship the sources never disclose and which has no counterpart among the connections FIG. 3 enumerates for the edge controller; and (2) FIG-1.md carries an internal cross-figure note ("FIG. 2 shows the coupling by which the edge controller reads a connector current sensor.") that specifies no FIG. 1 line work. Both have removal-only fixes that add nothing to the disclosure. The prior art supplied for the Background may be incomplete; Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to inventor sources, per the standing instruction.

findings.title: FIG. 2 depicts an undisclosed dedicated sensing path from the connector current sensor to the edge controller, drawn as crossing the isolated local bus without connecting to it
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, fifth and eighth line-work paragraphs (the downward line from the circle, and the bus paragraph); cross-checked against figures/FIG-3.md, fifth paragraph
findings.detail: The FIG. 2 brief creates a distinct signal path for reading the connector current sensor and then affirmatively separates it from the disclosed isolated local bus by having the bus cross it at a right angle with no junction. That is a connection/topology assertion with technical substance: it states that connector current readings do not travel on the isolated local bus but on a separate coupling that leaves the connector channel. The sources support only that a coupling of some kind exists (the controller 'verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor') and that the bus carries traffic to the 'connector interfaces and contactors'; no passage says how the current sensors are read, whether that path is separate from the bus, or that it crosses the bus. The same brief also anchors the control-pilot interface block's position to this undisclosed line ('to the right of that downward line'). The assertion is additionally not internally consistent: FIG. 3 enumerates the connections leaving the edge controller and provides only two descending lines, 'the connection leaving the edge controller to the isolated local bus' and 'the connection leaving the edge controller to the branch current sensor', so the FIG. 2 sensing line terminates free with no counterpart at the controller anywhere in the drawing set. A schematic sensor symbol in series in the power path with no signal line asserts nothing and is the neutral depiction; the description text is already neutral ('The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124') and needs no change.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): 'A straight solid vertical line leaves the lower side of that circle, runs downward, crosses the lower side of the dashed rectangle and ends free a short distance beneath it. It represents the coupling by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensor and carries no reference numeral of its own.' and 'Inside the rectangle this bus line continues to the right at that same height, crosses the downward sensing line at a right angle, and meets the left side of the control-pilot interface block.' and 'An empty rectangular block sits in the lower region of the dashed rectangle, to the right of that downward line and to the left of the vehicle connector block, and represents the control-pilot interface.' Cross-check (figures/FIG-3.md): 'The left one is solid along its whole length and represents the connection leaving the edge controller to the isolated local bus. The right one is dashed along its whole length and represents the connection leaving the edge controller to the branch current sensor.' No affirmative inventor passage describes how the controller reads a connector current sensor or what path that reading takes. Nearest source passages, which show the gap: 'A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.' and 'The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.' (input/disclosure.md, paragraphs 1 and 2).
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, delete the entire paragraph beginning 'A straight solid vertical line leaves the lower side of that circle'. In the bus paragraph, delete the clause 'crosses the downward sensing line at a right angle,' so the sentence reads 'Inside the rectangle this bus line continues to the right at that same height and meets the left side of the control-pilot interface block.' In the control-pilot paragraph, delete 'to the right of that downward line and' so the sentence reads 'An empty rectangular block sits in the lower region of the dashed rectangle, to the left of the vehicle connector block, and represents the control-pilot interface.' Make no change to figures/FIG-3.md and no change to draft/08-detailed-description.md; do not add any sensing line, bus tap, or junction to any figure.

findings.title: Internal cross-figure note left inside the FIG. 1 drawing brief
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, paragraph beginning 'A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block', final sentence
findings.detail: The sentence is an explanatory note about the content of a different figure. It specifies no line work, shape, numeral, or leader for FIG. 1, so it cannot be rendered and serves only as an internal comment explaining why the connector-sensor coupling is absent from FIG. 1. No drafting note or internal comment may remain in the drawing specification, and the FIG. 1 brief already fixes the line count at each block ('Each of the leftmost and middle blocks meets exactly two lines'), so nothing depends on the sentence. Removing it changes no depicted structure and adds nothing to the disclosure.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): 'The rightmost block meets exactly one line: the vertical drop at its top edge. FIG. 2 shows the coupling by which the edge controller reads a connector current sensor.' The remainder of the brief is pure line-work instruction for FIG. 1; no other sentence in any of the four briefs describes another figure's content.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, delete the sentence 'FIG. 2 shows the coupling by which the edge controller reads a connector current sensor.' so the paragraph ends at 'The rightmost block meets exactly one line: the vertical drop at its top edge.' Leave draft/07-drawings.md unchanged.
